solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Recommends a party including very small titbits?

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration
V is the standard abbreviation for very
cates is an old word for delicacies or dainty morsels of food

explanation.surface: Someone at a gathering recommends serving tiny canapés.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is not a political group but a social do; the last chunk is an archaic word for delicacies, worth knowing for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate is to speak publicly in favour of something, which is what someone who recommends it does.

clue.text: Goddess with skill is luring them in

blocks.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation
'em is the casual short form of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A goddess uses her skill to tempt mortals into her trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'luring them in' sounds like a container, but the shortened pronoun simply sits immediately before the final word, drawn in alongside it rather than inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting and the moon, sister of Apollo.

clue.text: The vehicle in front

blocks.note: first meaning: a covered road vehicle for goods
second meaning: the leading position

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about the car ahead; split it, and each half is a separate meaning of the same short word, the second short for vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a goods vehicle and, via vanguard, the foremost part of an army or movement.

clue.text: South Americans in church on island (is like Pisa’s tower)

blocks.note: CH is the usual abbreviation for church
I is the abbreviation for island
the tower at Pisa famously tilts

explanation.surface: Tourists from South America visit an island church with a tilting tower.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on' puts church above island; the bracketed aside is the final chunk, describing what the leaning tower does.
explanation.definitionFit: Chileans are the people of Chile, a country on South America's Pacific coast.

clue.text: Shift doctor’s ending with nurse around

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
to go around something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: to nurse is to tend or look after
the final letter of doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor finishes a shift and a nurse is on hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work period in a hospital, but it is the definition: a change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a general shift or movement in a particular direction, as in opinion or fashion.

clue.text: Son doing physical exercises — overdoing them?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
working out in a structured programme

explanation.surface: A son at the gym may be pushing himself too hard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: 'them' refers back to the exercises, and the question mark flags that the defining phrase is playful.
explanation.definitionFit: Straining means exerting yourself beyond comfort, which is what overdoing your workout amounts to.

clue.text: During course of day one gets quiet, blanked out?

indicators.note: something during a period falls within it, so the pieces are placed inside

blocks.note: Wed is the abbreviation for Wednesday
the Roman numeral for one
p, piano, is the musical instruction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Partway through a day someone goes silent and loses consciousness.
explanation.walkthrough: A day in crosswords is often a weekday abbreviation; here WED surrounds I and P.
explanation.definitionFit: A recording or memory that has been wiped is erased, blanked out completely, leaving nothing there.

clue.text: Plant one graduate noticed shooting up

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate
saw means noticed or spotted

explanation.surface: A student notices a plant growing rapidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting up' suits a plant, but in this down clue it turns the whole chain upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is a Japanese plant of the cabbage family whose pungent root makes the green condiment.

clue.text: Trip captain organised for one to join in?

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange into order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eleven letters used as written

explanation.surface: A captain sets up an outing and invites someone to come along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trip captain' reads as a tour leader, but the two words are simply the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A participant is someone who takes part in an activity, the person who joins in with others.

clue.text: Beast, this writer’s editor, set up as no mere mortal!

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means reading it from bottom to top

blocks.note: a dog is an animal, a beast
this writer is the setter, so 'this writer is' becomes I'M
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A writer grandly casts their own editor as a monster who is more than human.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this writer' is the crossword setter referring to themself, so with the apostrophe-s it gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: A demigod is a part-divine being, so by nature it is more than an ordinary mortal human.

clue.text: Financial scheme sound for saving money

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe within, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a tone is a musical sound
tin is old British slang for money

explanation.surface: A sound financial plan for putting money aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective meaning reliable, but it is a noun giving TONE; 'saving' is the container, not thrift.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontine is an investment arrangement in which subscribers pool money and the survivors take the shares of those who die.

clue.text: Platform where you see some hero’s trumpeted

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only a part of it, so the letters are found within

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A hero's arrival is announced with trumpets from a stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the apostrophe and the start of 'trumpeted'; the trumpeting suits a speaker's platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand from which a speaker or conductor addresses an audience.

clue.text: Plan to have the French national symbol

blocks.note: a map is a plan of an area
le is the French for the

explanation.surface: A proposal to adopt France's national emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French national symbol' suggests a cockerel or Marianne; 'the French' is just LE, and the symbol is Canada's.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple leaf is Canada's emblem, on its flag, so the tree serves as a national symbol.

clue.text: What makes airport seek new economic model?

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are given a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: the eleven letters used as written

explanation.surface: An airport looks for a fresh business plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The ending reads as 'seek a new economic model', but 'new' works on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Perestroika was Gorbachev's 1980s Soviet programme of restructuring the planned economy and political system.

clue.text: Robin maybe turning glitzy, acting like a football player?

indicators.note: turning round makes something face the other way, so its letters run backwards

blocks.note: a robin is an example of a bird
bling is flashy, showy jewellery or style

explanation.surface: Robin becoming flashy and showing off like a footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin looks like a person's name; 'maybe' marks it as an example of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Dribbling is moving the ball with repeated small touches past opponents, a core skill in soccer.

clue.text: Tiger seen moving? Not here, where lions are!

indicators.note: things that are moving shift position, so these letters change places

blocks.note: the nine letters used as written

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have seen a tiger roaming and is told tigers don't live there; lions do.
explanation.walkthrough: Tigers are Asian, so the African plain is precisely where no tiger is seen; that joke is why the definition opens 'Not here'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti is a vast Tanzanian savanna famous for its lion prides and migrating herds, with no wild tigers.

clue.text: Most jovial, but with husband descending to become most crude

indicators.note: to descend is to move lower, so in this down entry a letter drops further down the column

blocks.note: heartiest means most cheerful and exuberant
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A cheerful man's husband comes down and things turn very vulgar.
explanation.walkthrough: The H at the top of HEARTIEST slides down past four letters; nothing is added or lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and bawdy, so the superlative describes the most vulgar or unrefined.

clue.text: Moderate leader being upturned — uncivilized!

indicators.note: turning a letter upside down changes its shape into a different letter

blocks.note: mild means moderate, not extreme

explanation.surface: A moderate party leader is overthrown, and the result is savage.
explanation.walkthrough: An M flipped upside down looks like a W, so the first letter swaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Wild describes something untamed, savage and not living under civilized order.

clue.text: Sibling gaining promotion with style in NY location

blocks.note: bro is short for brother
an ad, advertisement, promotes a product
a way of doing something is its style or manner

explanation.surface: A brother wins promotion thanks to his flair at a New York firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' reads as a job rise but means advertising.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the long Manhattan avenue whose theatre district gives American stage drama its name.

clue.text: Son swamped by stream of water? It’s fun

indicators.note: something swamped is engulfed and covered, so one piece lies inside another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a jet is a forceful spurt of water

explanation.surface: A boy soaked by a water jet — and it's all in fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The S sits inside JET.
explanation.definitionFit: Jest is joking or playfulness, as in 'said in jest', meaning just for fun.

clue.text: Fair number wanting bit of work recently

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part, here its opening letter only

blocks.note: just means fair and impartial
No. is the abbreviation for number
the first letter of work

explanation.surface: A fair number of people wanted a little work lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair number' reads as 'quite a few', but the words split: Fair is one piece, number another; 'wanting' here means needing, adding the last piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something happened just now means it happened a very short time ago, a moment earlier.

clue.text: Ending in danger, say, a road worker looking back

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of danger
e.g., for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'
taken as written
Rd is the abbreviation for road
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A roadworker glances over his shoulder at the end of a hazardous job.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a heraldic term; build it from five small pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, a regardant beast is shown with its head turned to gaze backwards over its shoulder.

clue.text: Bird gets brown with time, right?

blocks.note: tan is a light brown colour
an age is a period of time
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bird's plumage darkens as it grows older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown' reads as a verb, as in browning with age, but it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanagers are small, often brilliantly coloured songbirds of the Americas, related to cardinals.

clue.text: Struggled to get supper finally into oven

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter is kept
going into something means ending up inside it

blocks.note: a stove is a cooker with an oven
the final letter of supper

explanation.surface: Someone battled to get the evening meal into the oven at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' reads as 'at last' in the story, but it picks out one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Strove is the past tense of strive, meaning made great effort or fought hard.

clue.text: What able person is up to with little hesitation, being a scorer?

blocks.clueFragment: What able person is up to
blocks.note: a capable person is 'up to scratch', meeting the standard
er is a brief hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A competent player, barely pausing, scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scorer' suggests goals, but to score is also to scratch a line or mark on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: One who scores a surface makes cuts or lines in it, which is exactly what a scratcher does.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed, I had performed again

blocks.note: an embarrassed face goes red
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Blushing, a performer confesses to having done the act a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are a colour and a contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo something is to carry it out once more, so redid is did a second time.

clue.text: Affect part of London

blocks.note: first meaning: a two-word phrasal verb for influencing something
second meaning: a district in west London

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is a phrasal verb; as one word it is a place name.
explanation.definitionFit: To act on something is to influence it; Acton is also a suburb in the borough of Ealing.

clue.text: Is duck invading old Greek region offensive?

indicators.note: an invader moves inside territory, so these pieces go within another

blocks.note: taken as written
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O
a nome was a province of ancient Greece or Egypt

explanation.surface: Is a duck straying into ancient Greek territory an affront?
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a duck is a batter's score of nothing; NOME is a rare word for an ancient administrative district.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisome means foul-smelling or highly disagreeable, so it is close to offensive or repugnant.

clue.text: There’s flooding with river unwanted in Cambridge college

indicators.note: what is unwanted is thrown out, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: flooding as in a person swamped and drowning
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college suffers floods, and nobody wants the river there.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the R out of DROWNING.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing College is one of the constituent colleges of Cambridge University, founded in 1800.

clue.text: Regularly fierce, showing strong emotion

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone habitually fierce displays powerful feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the even letters of the word after the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is anger or wrath, a powerful feeling, so strong emotion is a fair if broad description.

clue.text: Wife, healthy swimmer with lots of blubber!

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
hale means robust and healthy

explanation.surface: A fit, plump wife out for a swim — perhaps crying a lot too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blubber' hints at sobbing, but it is the thick fat of a sea mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: Whales are huge marine mammals insulated by a thick layer of fat known as blubber.

clue.text: Dry bed at start of evening — somehow it may help child rest?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept
somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters fall into an unpredictable new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter of evening

explanation.surface: At bedtime a dry bed and something comforting help a child sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is part of the anagram fodder despite reading as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft toy bear is the classic comforter a young child cuddles to settle down to sleep.
